segments.translation_text: There are five aspects of morality: eternal morality, which is preserving morality until enlightenment is reached; naturally arisen morality, which is the arising of moral actions due to familiarization; morality of complete non-violence, which is the accomplishment of the path and activities of the ten wholesome actions; morality of personal delight, which is the realization that one possesses good qualities; and the morality of heedfulness, which is always abiding in the non-deluded state.

segments.translation_text: The opposite of morality that should be discarded is all types of corrupt morality, the nature of which is non-virtuous. The antidote is realization of the selflessness of phenomena, through which one possesses primordial wisdom of non-conceptualization of the three cycles. The outcome that is a temporary result is pure morality which benefits other beings through body, voice, and mind and fulfills all their wishes. The ultimate result is placing sentient beings in the nirvana of one of the three vehicles according to their motivation. Thus beings are completely matured through the four dharmas.

segments.translation_text: Meaningful nature means to possess the six branches which are: possess morality as described above; bind oneself by the pratimoksha vows; perfect ritual; environment; regard even the smallest faults with fear; and train completely in the precepts that one has undertaken. The meaningful cause is a mind that seizes the desire to attain the peace of liberation in nirvana. The meaningful result is temporarily taking higher rebirth without regret, etc., and ultimately becoming able to engage the mind in single-pointed absorption. Meaningful action is the base of all good qualities, pacification of the mental weariness of the defilements, and freedom from the fear of harming others. Meaningful possession means that throughout the three times, the body, voice, and mind engage only in perfect actions, so one possesses a heap of merit.

segments.translation_text: A complete classification of meaningful engagement follows. The morality of the desire realm is the wish to discard harm to others as well as its base. It is practiced through pratimoksha vows, which are obtained through a symbolic ritual. The morality of the form realm is the wish to simultaneously discard the contaminated meditation of the six types of meditative absorption, which is known as the vow obtained from meditative absorption. The uncontaminated morality pleasing to the Noble Ones is the wish to discard the simultaneously arising uncontaminated meditative absorption, which is known as the vow obtained from suchness. A practitioner who possesses these various vows has a base of meaningful engagement.

segments.translation_text: One may think, "If a downfall occurs I can confess it and take the vow again.” However, giving up the Bodhisattva vow is a powerful downfall, and taking the Bodhisattva vow is a powerful virtue. segments.translation_text: From another point of view, for the time being my body is healthy and without illness like the sun, and I have food and clothing and the other necessities. segments.translation_text: Some who fight for meaningless purposes enter the battlefield, are injured by the enemy, and receive scars on their foreheads. segments.translation_text: The defilements that need to be abandoned are abandoned by the antidote which is the understanding of their lack of inherent nature through the analytical eye of wisdom. Worldly wisdom abandons them by suppressing the seed of the defilements, and beyond-worldly wisdom abandons them by uprooting the seed itself. If the seed itself is uprooted, nothing can return. If I had these, the defilements would be easier to conquer than any other enemies because they do not have any inherent nature.
